NDVI_Models

Matt Webster

2026-07-28

The purpose of this RMarkdown is to implement hierarchical generalized linear mixed effects models for NDVI ~ damPresence, & NDVI ~ damDensity (with and without geomorphic covariates). Structurally parallel to all other hurdle/HGLMM models for Ch1.

4 models total.

Rough normality of NDVI distribution does not require response transformation prior
to modeling.

For NDVI models, data of interest include:

 - NDVI: average NDVI for sample window[i]; response variable

- stream: index for random intercept on NDVI and random slope on dam effect

- year: index for random slope on dam effect

- sampleEvent: index for random intercept on NDVI and random slope on dam effect 
  (nested within year; represents each 2 week sample period for Veg layer )

- clusterID_seq: index for random intercept on NDVI; represents sample pairing

- damPres: dam presence (0,1); fixed effect on NDVI

- damDen: dams/km; z-standardized ("...$dam_km_std"); fixed effect on NDVI

Only used in models 2 and 4:

- incis: channel incision: 1-(TO/90) (inverse of topographic openness); z-standardized;
  fixed effect on NDVI

- RIPA: riparian area (m^2); z-standardized; fixed effect on NDVI 

- UDA: upstream drainage area (km ^2); z-standardized; fixed effect on NDVI

HGLMM

This analysis explores late summer vegetation greenness (NDVI) in relation to 
beaver dam presence, & density.

2 models for dam presence (1 without geomorphic covariates; 1 with geomorphic covariates)
2 models for dam density (...^^^...)

All 4 models presented herein are constructed in a hierarchical generalized linear mixed
effects model framework with nested random slopes for beaver dam effect to allow
for stream, year, and sampleEvent to cause deviation from the global mean beaver
effect. Stream, sampleEvent, and sample clusterID are also included as random intercepts
for baseline NDVI. 

  - NDVI ~ damPresence (no geom.covar.)
  - NDVI ~ damPresence (geom.covar.)
  - NDVI ~ damDensity (no geom.covar.)
  - NDVI ~ damDensity (no geom.covar.)

Model structure is paralleled with HGLMMs for veg area.

Uses mean(NDVI) for each sample window for 6 watersheds, 3 years, 4 sample periods 
(Aug-Sep) per year.

Overall Takeaways

...

RANDOM SLOPE STRUCTURE FOR DAM EFFECT IS TOO COMPLEX FOR NDVI DATA.
Almost no group-level variation in NDVI. Complex random effects structure collapses.

TRY SIMPLER MODEL.
Simplify by removing random slopes, as well as random intercept event -- not enough 
group-level variation to support these random effects. Maintain random intercepts
for stream, year, and cluster.

Illustrated below:

...

When we simplify the model, we see that:

Dams have positive, though MARGINAL effect on NDVI.

## m1_mu_NDVI_post 
##        1.037244
Comparison of model-estimated NDVI with observed NDVI. "Perfect" model fit would
have a slope = 1. A slope of 1.03 is very reasonable, given model. This indicates
that our model for NDVI is performing fairly well.

Random effects shrinkage:

Should be centered around 0(ish)

  1. eta_stream; random effect of stream on NDVI intercept (1:6)
  2. eta_year; random effect of year on NDVI intercept (1:3)

NDVI ~ damPres (no geom.covar.)

##     Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max. 
## 0.003116 0.008738 0.009858 0.009865 0.010978 0.016678

Without consideration of geomorphic covariates, dam presence is associated with a
~0.01 increase in NDVI. No overlap of zero. Confidently, a very meager effect.
